Bulldog Beacon

Lux et Securitas

Campus safety for the Yale community: one-tap SOS, walk-home check-ins, a fair and calm community board, and an AI assistant that knows Yale.

Jeffrey Bosmediano · MGT 409 AI Foundations for Managers · Fall 2026
https://github.com/Jbosmediano683/bulldog-beacon
Student project; not an official Yale service.

The problem

  • 33,366 people study or work at Yale. Many walk to cars, garages, and trains after dark. One is my wife, who works night shifts at YCCI.
  • October 2026: a Yale officer fired into a car next to Evans Hall during a crisis call, and a Yale employee was shot at 4 a.m. arriving at work.
  • Yale's services are good, but they're spread across many pages, and even the escort number appears two different ways.
  • Public apps mix real reports with rumor and profiling, and they leave people more anxious.

SOS and check-ins never wait for AI. Real Yale events and good news keep it from being all bad news.

How the agents work

Four gpt-6-luna agents with one job each. Code routes the work and checks every answer. The Moderator, which reads untrusted text, gets no tools.

Demo: a post, checked and merged

Race and the license plate removed before posting. A matching report merged into "2 separate reports." A comment that attacked homeless people blocked, with the reason shown only to its author.

Demo: the walk to the car

She asks Beacon about the route, misses her check-in, and holds SOS. The alert goes out instantly; AI only writes the dispatcher's summary afterward.

Safety

83/83offline checks pass
23/23live attacks stopped
100%on unseen posts
0AI steps in SOS
  • Rules, then agent, then guards: verified phone numbers only, citations checked, fail closed
  • Stops profiling, doxxing, rumors, threats, and direct and indirect prompt injection
  • Limits: 8 AI calls a minute and 150k tokens a day per NetID, plus an app-wide cap. The load test found 20 simultaneous chats slipping past; fixed, now 8 of 20 get through.

Impact

  • 33,366 people who could use it; about $124.63 a month in AI cost if every one of them did
  • One tap to a Yale Security walking escort, instead of searching pages that disagree
  • In tests, every profiling post was blocked or rewritten (Nextdoor's form: 75% fewer)
  • About 25 Yale events a day on the same map, so the app isn't all bad news
  • Rehearsal with 8 AI personas (not people): 24/24 goals met, and 4 problems they exposed are fixed

Real user: My wife (YCCI night shifts) tried it on her phone. Her finding: Walk With Me had to start from your current location, not a list. Fixed the same day.
